Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'll keep us tight today, this is the week where we want to close the business case and make sure procurement has what they need. Ethan, quick status on the tuning side?
[00:18] Ethan: Yeah, hi. So last 48 hours we pushed the 4-bit quantized config on the testrun cluster, so token cost dropped ~33% on average. Latency median held about 120 ms, p95 jumped to ~540 ms in our longest sequences — that's with the new batching heuristics. Some spike behavior on cold KV-cache misses, but we documented it.
[00:45] Ruth: Can you repeat the p95 number? Sorry, the call audio is a bit rough.
[00:51] Ethan: p95 ~540 ms, p99 around 920 ms in the heaviest queries. Median 120.
[01:08] Derek: Those are within our SLO? We had earlier said median <150ms and p95 <600 is acceptable.
[01:15] Maya: Correct, and Ruth you previously flagged throughput as more important than tail for batch inference on reporting flows — is that still the case?
[01:23] Ruth: Yes for the nightly report jobs throughput matters, but for interactive triage (support workflows) we need sub-500ms p95. So p95 of 540 means we need to tune a little more for that use-case.
[01:35] Priya: Quick context — our product owners will accept 550ms for triage if our accuracy lifts are consistent. The financial side cares more about token cost reduction.
[01:45] Samir: And finance will need the pro-forma showing savings vs our existing hosted vendor baseline. We can't sign anything without a line-item comparison.
[01:55] Angela: Also procurement needs SOC2 Type II evidence and a sample contract with data handling clauses; please send anything that helps speed review.
[02:05] Maya: Totally — we'll attach the SOC2 summary and our standard DPA. We'll also include the performance workbook with token-level breakdown.
[02:14] Ethan: On the accuracy front we ran the domain prompts set A and saw a +6.8% F1 lift versus baseline model and vt. Some of the edge cases still error — mostly long-form instruction following.
[02:30] Ruth: Did you try the alternative reranking flow? Last week you mentioned a reranker to boost precision.
[02:36] Ethan: We did a light rerank after generation for the last two runs. It improved precision by about 3 points but added ~40ms to median latency. For interactive flows I can look at a cached-kv approach to reduce that overhead.
[02:50] Ruth: Ok that might be acceptable if it keeps p95 <500ms.
[02:58] Maya: Let's put that as a tuning item for Ethan this week — can you try cached-kv + reduced rerank window?
[03:05] Ethan: Yup, will do.

[07:12] Derek: On infra model — if we move to Dedicated, what's the lead time for capacity? We need predictable throughput for weekly reports.
[07:20] Maya: Dedicated onboarding lead time is typically 3 weeks after PO and network details; if you're going Private on-prem it's more like 6-8 weeks depending on procurement of machines and network approvals.
[07:34] Angela: So to hit an August start we'd need PO signed by end of July?
[07:40] Maya: That's right, end of July for a tentative early August onboarding.

[10:05] Samir: Finance question — the cost modeling we saw had variable ranges. Can you give a committed-commit pricing example vs pay-as-you-go? We need to show savings over our current vendor with a 12-month horizon.
[10:17] Maya: We will send a final worksheet with three scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go, 6-month committed Dedicated, and 12-month committed Dedicated. Each will show token cost, estimated infra, and predicted savings vs your current baseline. We'll also highlight break-evens.
[10:27] Samir: Great, include assumptions for request volume, average sequence length, and caching hit rates. Those drove a lot of delta in our earlier numbers.
[10:36] Ethan: Noted — we'll attach the exact run parameters used in the benchmark (batch sizes, sequence length distribution, cache hit %).

[13:40] Ruth: On compliance, a quick question — we have to keep PHI out of logs. Will Redwood redact or can we route logs to our own S3 for retention?
[13:50] Maya: You can disable logging for specific routes and use private log forwarding to your S3; we also support customer-managed keys so logs encrypted with your KMS are available only to you.
[13:59] Angela: We'll need the KMS integration docs and a note about audit log retention times.
[14:06] Maya: We'll include that in the security appendix we send later today.

[18:12] Priya: Back to success criteria — Ruth, can you read the proposed thresholds so we align?
[18:18] Ruth: Sure. For the pilot to be considered a success: 1) Average accuracy (F1) >= 0.82 on our validation set; 2) Median latency <150ms for interactive routes and p95 <500ms after tuning; 3) Token cost reduction >= 25% vs current baseline; 4) No critical security gaps found in SOC2/DPA review.
[18:39] Maya: That maps cleanly to what we measured — accuracy hit 0.83 on the last run, median 120ms, p95 540ms (so we need to get p95 below 500), cost reduction 33% on the quantized run. So only p95 remains outstanding.
[18:55] Ruth: Ok, so action item is p95 tuning.

[21:10] Derek: One procurement question — do we lock model version in contract? We want reproducible outputs across billing cycles.
[21:18] Ethan: You can pin model version at deployment. Redwood supports model version pinning and rollouts; we also provide model provenance logs for QA. If you opt for Dedicated we can keep the runtime fixed and only upgrade by mutual agreement.
[21:35] Samir: And rollback process? If we see a regression after rollout, what's the support SLA?
[21:40] Maya: We have rollback tooling and can revert within the hour for emergencies; SLA for critical incidents is 1 hour response and business-impacting mitigations, we can put specifics in the contract.

[24:50] Angela: On legal redlines — we'll need the DPA and our standard security addendum back. Can Redwood accept our 60-day notice for export controls?
[24:59] Maya: We'll review the addendum and flag any exceptions; we'll aim to return redline comments within 3 business days.

[27:05] Ruth: Ethan, one technical ask — can you share the exact prompt templates and normalization steps you used? We want to ensure parity before we roll into production.
[27:15] Ethan: Yes, I'll upload the prompt templates and the normalization scripts plus the seed set used for evaluation (sanitized).

[30:00] Priya: For stakeholder signoff, we need a simple one-pager summarizing the achievements vs success criteria for executive review. Can Redwood provide that?
[30:09] Maya: Yes, we'll do an exec one-pager — topline metrics, cost delta, and risks.
[30:15] Priya: Please keep it very short — CFO will look at cost and risk only.

[33:22] Samir: If the numbers show a clear >20% cost reduction with acceptable latency, finance is likely to recommend a 12-month commitment. What's the discount tier for 12-month?
[33:31] Maya: We have standard tiering; for a 12-month commit we typically apply a 15-25% discount depending on committed QPS and seat-level services. We'll put a model-specific estimate in the worksheet.

[36:40] Ruth: Small note — some of the edge-case failures we saw were hallucinations around company-specific jargon. Can we add a small post-filter or fallback?
[36:50] Ethan: We already implemented a lightweight fallback where low-confidence outputs route to a deterministic retrieval flow — that reduced hallucination incidents by half. There is a small latency cost but we can gate it on confidence thresholds.
[37:04] Ruth: Good, let's keep that for the triage flows.

[40:00] Angela: From procurement — what's required to start a Dedicated trial? What do you need from us?
[40:09] Maya: Short answer: signed SOW/PO, network details (VPC peering or customer VPC endpoint), and the list of admin users. We'll also need the contract countersigned and your billing contacts.
[40:20] Angela: Ok we'll try to get that by 2025-07-25.

[43:12] Maya: Quick recap and next steps: Redwood to send performance + cost workbook, SOC2 summary, security appendix, DPA and sample SOW; Ethan to run p95 tuning with cached-kv + rerank window reduction and share configs; Ruth to confirm final success thresholds; Angela to share procurement timeline. Everyone good?
[43:28] Derek: Sounds good.
[43:31] Ruth: Fine with me.
[43:33] Samir: Fine.
[43:35] Angela: Fine.
[43:37] Priya: Thanks all.
[43:40] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in writing and drop the worksheet by Monday.
